places.name: Munnar
places.summary: Kerala's tea country at around 1,600 m: rolling estates, Eravikulam's Nilgiri tahr, lakes, viewpoints and treks.
places.seoTitle: Munnar Travel Guide: Tea Estates, Viewpoints & Treks
places.seoDescription: Plan a Munnar trip: tea estates and the Tea Museum, Eravikulam, Mattupetty, Top Station and Kolukkumalai, treks, the monsoon and how to get there from Kochi.

images.alt: Rolling tea plantations on the hills of Munnar

overview.text:
Munnar sits at around 1,600 m in the Western Ghats of Idukki district, where three rivers meet. Its hills are carpeted with tea estates that date back to the late 19th century, when the British turned the area into a planting district.

The cool climate, with temperatures of about 5–25 °C, draws visitors all year. Eravikulam National Park, home of the endangered Nilgiri tahr and the Neelakurinji flower that blooms once every 12 years, is next door. Viewpoints such as Mattupetty and Top Station, the lakes and waterfalls, and treks to Anamudi, South India's highest peak, fill the days. It suits couples, families and walkers.

items.title: Getting there
items.body: About 130 km from Kochi on NH 49. The nearest major railway stations are Aluva (110 km) and Ernakulam (126 km), with KSRTC buses to Munnar from near Aluva.

items.title: Climate
items.body: Cool all year (about 5–25 °C). Pack layers.

items.title: Monsoon
items.body: June–September brings heavy rain. Allow extra time on the ghat roads.

items.title: Couples
items.body: Misty viewpoints, tea-estate walks and lakeside picnics.

items.title: Families
items.body: Boating at Mattupetty and Kundala, and the Tea Museum.

items.title: Trekkers
items.body: Anamudi, Meesapulimala and the Kolukkumalai estate.

items.title: Wildlife lovers
items.body: The Nilgiri tahr at Eravikulam, Chinnar and the Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary.
Trying Top Station, Kolukkumalai and Eravikulam in one day. They lie in different directions on slow hill roads.
Packing only for the tropics. Munnar can drop to about 5 °C.
Expecting the Neelakurinji every year. It blooms only once every 12 years.

items.title: How far is Munnar from Kochi?
items.body: About 130 km, on the Kochi–Dhanushkodi highway (NH 49).

items.title: Is there a train to Munnar?
items.body: No. The old Kunda Valley Railway was destroyed by a flood in 1924. Take a train to Aluva or Ernakulam and continue by road.

items.title: When does the Neelakurinji bloom?
items.body: Once every 12 years, on the slopes of Eravikulam.

items.title: Is Munnar good in the monsoon?
items.body: It's green but very wet from June to September, with slow roads. Allow extra time.

places.name: Tata Tea Museum
places.summary: Museum of Munnar's tea history with antique processing machinery.
places.seoTitle: Tata Tea Museum, Munnar: Tea History
places.seoDescription: Munnar's Tata Tea Museum traces the history of tea in the High Ranges, with antique tea-processing machinery and exhibits on how tea is made.

images.alt: Entrance of the Tea Museum in Munnar with gardens

overview.text:
The Tata Tea Museum tells the story of tea cultivation in Munnar, from the late 19th-century estates to today. It displays antique tea-processing equipment and exhibits on the tea industry, and it is a good introduction before walking the estates themselves.

Combine it with a guided tea-factory or plantation tour to see how the leaf you saw on the hillside becomes the tea in your cup. It is a short trip from the town centre and a good rainy-day option.

items.body: Visit early in your trip to make sense of the estates you'll see.
Buy tea to take home from the museum's shop or local estate outlets.
Allow about an hour.
Ask whether a short film or demonstration is running when you arrive.
Combine with a tea-factory tour on an estate nearby.

places.name: Kolukkumalai
places.summary: One of the world's highest tea estates, famed for sunrise above the clouds.
places.seoTitle: Kolukkumalai, Munnar: High Tea Estate & Sunrise
places.seoDescription: Kolukkumalai near Munnar is one of the highest tea plantations in the world, with century-old tea bushes and dramatic sunrise views over the ranges.

images.alt: Tea slopes and peaks at Kolukkumalai near Munnar

overview.text:
Kolukkumalai, near Munnar, is one of the highest tea plantations in the world, and some of its tea bushes are more than a century old. It is best known for sunrise: arrive before dawn and watch the light break over the ranges and the clouds below.

The estate sits high above the valleys, so plan transport up the night before and set off in the dark. It's a magical start to a Munnar day, and the century-old tea bushes are a sight in themselves once the sun is up.

items.body: Book a jeep the night before and set off well before dawn.
Bring warm layers and a torch; it is cold before sunrise.
Ask your hotel to arrange transport; the estate road is steep and narrow.

places.name: Mattupetty Dam and Lake
places.summary: Reservoir and viewpoint near Munnar, popular for boating and picnics.
places.seoDescription: Mattupetty, near Munnar, is one of its best-known viewpoints, with a lake popular for boating and picnics among the hills.

images.alt: Mattupetty lake between forested hills near Munnar

overview.text: Mattupetty is one of Munnar's best-known viewpoints, and its lake is one of the area's favourites for boating and picnics, along with Kundala and Devikulam. It is usually combined with Echo Point and Kundala on the road towards Top Station.

places.name: Top Station
places.summary: High viewpoint near Munnar with sweeping views over the Western Ghats.
places.seoDescription: Top Station is one of Munnar's popular viewpoints, with sweeping views over the hills and valleys of the Western Ghats on clear mornings.

images.alt: Ridges and valleys seen from Top Station near Munnar

overview.text: Top Station is one of Munnar's popular viewpoints, with panoramic views over the hills and valleys of the Western Ghats. Go early: mist and cloud often roll in later in the day. It's at the end of the scenic road past Mattupetty and Echo Point.

places.name: Alappuzha (Alleppey)
places.summary: The 'Venice of the East': backwater houseboats, canals and paddy fields, the beach pier and the Nehru Trophy Boat Race.
places.seoTitle: Alleppey (Alappuzha) Guide: Houseboats, Beach & Boat Race
places.seoDescription: Plan an Alleppey trip: backwater houseboats, Alappuzha Beach and pier, the Nehru Trophy Boat Race (second Saturday of August), Kerala food and getting there.

images.alt: A kettuvallam houseboat on the backwaters near Alappuzha

overview.text:
Alappuzha, better known as Alleppey, lies about 62 km south of Kochi on Kerala's coast. Lord Curzon called it the 'Venice of the East'. Its heart is the backwaters: a maze of canals, lakes and lagoons through coconut groves and paddy fields, best seen from a traditional houseboat.

The town also has a long beach with a pier more than 137 years old, a coir-making heritage and temples such as Ambalapuzha, known for its palpayasam. In August, the Nehru Trophy Boat Race fills Punnamada Lake with 100-foot snake boats. It suits couples, families and anyone who wants to slow down.

items.title: Couples
items.body: An overnight houseboat through the backwaters, and sunset at the beach pier.

items.title: Festival-goers
items.body: The Nehru Trophy Boat Race in August, and the Adoor Gajamela elephant festival in January.

items.title: Food lovers
items.body: Karimeen pollichathu, seafood and banana-leaf breakfasts.

items.title: Culture seekers
items.body: Ambalapuzha temple and the coir heritage.
Coir products, from the town's long-standing coir industry.
Banana chips and fried banana snacks to take home.

items.title: Getting there
items.body: About 62 km south of Kochi. Alappuzha station, on the coastal line, is about 4 km from the centre.

items.title: Boat race
items.body: The Nehru Trophy is on the second Saturday of August. Book rooms early.
Booking the cheapest houseboat without checking licences and reviews. Use registered operators.
Spending only a few hours on the water. An overnight cruise shows the backwaters at their best.
Arriving on race weekend without a booking.

items.title: How far is Alleppey from Kochi?
items.body: About 62 km south.

items.title: When is the Nehru Trophy Boat Race?
items.body: The second Saturday of August each year, on Punnamada Lake.

items.title: Is there a railway station?
items.body: Yes, on the Ernakulam–Kayamkulam coastal line, about 4 km from the centre.

items.title: What should I eat?
items.body: Karimeen pollichathu (pearl spot fish in banana leaf), fresh seafood, and puttu with chickpea curry.

places.name: Alappuzha Beach
places.summary: Alleppey's favourite picnic beach, with a pier stretching into the sea for over 137 years.
places.seoTitle: Alappuzha Beach & Pier: Sunsets in Alleppey
places.seoDescription: Alappuzha Beach is the city's favourite picnic spot, with a historic pier stretching into the Arabian Sea for over 137 years and fine sunsets.

images.alt: The old pier at Alappuzha Beach silhouetted at sunset

overview.text:
Alappuzha Beach is the city's most popular spot for picnics and relaxing. Its historic pier has stretched into the sea for more than 137 years, a reminder of the port Alleppey once was. Evenings are the time to come, when families gather on the sand and the sun sets over the Arabian Sea behind the pier.

It is close to the town centre and easy to combine with a backwater cruise earlier in the day. Weekday evenings are calmer than weekends.

items.body: Come for sunset and stay for snacks from the beach stalls.
The sea can be rough, so swim only where it is safe and lifeguards are present.
Keep off the old pier structure where it is fenced.
Bring water and sun protection for daytime visits.

places.name: Nehru Trophy Boat Race
places.summary: Kerala's most famous snake-boat race on Punnamada Lake, held the second Saturday of August.
places.seoTitle: Nehru Trophy Boat Race, Alleppey: Date & Tips
places.seoDescription: Watch 100-foot snake boats race on Punnamada Lake in the Nehru Trophy Boat Race, held in Alappuzha on the second Saturday of August every year.

images.alt: A long snake boat with dozens of rowers racing at the Nehru Trophy, Alappuzha

overview.text:
The Nehru Trophy Boat Race is Alappuzha's great event. On Punnamada Lake, 100-foot-long chundan vallams (snake boats) race each other, each driven by hundreds of rowers pulling in perfect time. The air is electric with cheering and the drumming that sets the rowers' rhythm.

It is held on the second Saturday of August every year. Plan well ahead: it is the busiest weekend of the year in Alappuzha, and the lakeside gets packed with spectators from early in the day.

items.body: Book race-day tickets and rooms weeks ahead.
Arrive early to get a good spot by the water.
Carry an umbrella: August is the monsoon.
Watch the practice runs on the days before if you can't get race-day seats.
Keep valuables secure in the crowds.

places.name: Ambalapuzha Sri Krishna Temple
places.summary: Krishna temple near Alappuzha known for its palpayasam, sweet milk porridge offered to the deity.
places.seoDescription: Ambalapuzha Sri Krishna Temple near Alappuzha is famous for its palpayasam, a sweet milk porridge offered to the deity, and its Kerala temple architecture.

images.commons: File:Ambalappuzha Sri Krishna Temple Kerala Hinduism India.jpg
images.alt: Ambalapuzha Sri Krishna Temple with its pond and Kerala-style roofs

overview.text:
The Sri Krishna temple at Ambalapuzha, south of Alappuzha, is one of Kerala's best-known temples, in the classic Kerala style of tiled roofs and wooden halls. It is famous for its palpayasam, a sweet milk porridge offered to the deity, which devotees take home as prasadam.

It is an easy drive from Alappuzha and can be combined with a beach evening or a backwater trip. Mornings are usually the calmest time to visit, before the day's heat.

items.body: Kerala temples often have dress codes, and some inner areas may be closed to visitors. Follow the notices and staff at the gate.
Leave footwear outside and keep phones away inside the shrine.
Ask at the counter about buying palpayasam.
Dress modestly and cover your shoulders and knees.

itineraries.seoDescription: A two-day Munnar plan: the Tea Museum and estates, Mattupetty, Echo Point and Top Station, then Eravikulam's Nilgiri tahr. Getting there from Kochi.

plan.overview: From Kochi (about 130 km). Day 1 follows the Top Station road; day 2 is Eravikulam and a quieter afternoon. Monsoon (June–September) roads are slow.

days.title: Tea and the Top Station road

alternatives: Fit early risers: swap day 2's morning for sunrise at Kolukkumalai.
